_comment: Corrections to extracted quotes, keyed by guest_slug then film_id. Quotes are generated by the LLM pass in extract_quotes.py, so an entry here contradicts it on purpose and must cite transcript evidence in its note. Set "quote" to a verbatim passage from the guest's own transcript, or to null to clear a quote that belongs to a different pick. Applied by extract_quotes.py after every run, so a re-extraction cannot silently revert the correction. Two kinds of defect qualify: the model attributed one utterance to the wrong film, or it truncated an utterance mid-thought and dropped the words that complete it. In the second case the replacement may also drop filler and asides, marking every cut with an ellipsis. The hard limit either way is that every word must be verbatim from that guest's transcript -- this file re-cuts what the guest said, it never rewrites it. NOT for polishing wording the model got right, and NOT for the ordinary case where a guest genuinely covers several films in one breath, which is legitimate and common.

roma-1972.quote: Now, Fellini. I love Amarcord, I love all his neorealism period and all that. But this movie and Casanova are the ones I revisit the most. I remember one of my favorite scenes ever committed to film, I won't ruin it for you, is the scene where they discover the frescoes in the subway. Watch it. And there are moments here where the music and the staging, the sort of fashion design for Cardinals, the way that whole set piece works is like a horror movie.
roma-1972.note: Both Roma entries -- Fellini's 1972 film and Cuaron's 2018 one -- were given the same quote, which is entirely about Cuaron's: 'Alfonso had been talking about making this movie... for about 20 years.' The transcript shows del Toro discussing Fellini's Roma from 193s, naming the frescoes in the subway and the fashion show for Cardinals, both scenes from the 1972 film, and only then saying at 227s 'Oh, I found another Roma that I like' as he moves to Cuaron's. The passage restored here is his verbatim Fellini section; the Cuaron quote stays on roma-2018.

salvatore-giuliano.note: This carried Salo's words, not its own. The transcript reads 'last time I was here it was 2009 and I said that this movie was a good date movie uh solo my favorite part of this movie is when um and then the guy he goes into a room and he finds his plate of it is not a good date movie just want to clear that up'. 'Solo' is the captioner mishearing 'Salo', and the man who goes into a room and finds his plate of excrement is Salo, not Salvatore Giuliano. The model inserted the words 'Salvatore Giuliano.' into the passage to fit the pick it was asked about. The same utterance already sits on salo-or-the-120-days-of-sodom, where it belongs, so this one is cleared.

salo-or-the-120-days-of-sodom.quote: Last time I was here it was 2009 and I said that this movie was a good date movie. Salò. My favorite part of this movie is when... and then the guy, he goes into a room and he finds his plate of... It is not a good date movie, just want to clear that up.
salo-or-the-120-days-of-sodom.note: Came from the audio fallback and shipped raw: 'Said that this movie was a good date movie solo my favorite part of this movie is when and then the guy he goes into a room...' -- opening clause missing, no punctuation, and 'solo' where the captioner misheard 'Salo'. Restored to the transcript's own wording with the sentence breaks the clean step would normally add. Nothing is added that he did not say.

charulata.quote: I stole many things for my own movies from Ray… Charulata, they translate it as The Lonely Wife, she spends much of her time looking out from the rooms in her house with binoculars. And for my film Moonrise Kingdom… we’ve got a lot of binocular shots, only because of Satyajit Ray.
charulata.note: The extraction stopped at 118.45s ("with binoculars") and dropped the sentence that completes the thought, at 120.12-128s: "And for my film Moonrise Kingdom, which is out here somewhere, we've got a lot of binocular shots, only because of Satyajit Ray, one of my favorite great masters of cinema." Charulata's heroine watches the world through binoculars and Moonrise Kingdom is full of binocular shots -- Anderson is naming a specific thing he took from Ray, and without that sentence the quote is a setup with its payoff cut off. Restored, and trimmed of filler he talks through on the way there ("Okay, this is a good one to end on", the "one of the best... maybe the best" self-repair, "and this one, this woman...", "which is out here somewhere"). Every word is verbatim from the oJXKHJeVav0 transcript; ellipses mark the cuts. start_timestamp moved 99 -> 106 to land on the new first words.
